channel.title: TribalGaming.com — News & Analysis
channel.description: Authoritative news and analysis of tribal gaming in the United States and Canada.

item.title: Oklahoma tribal sports betting bill HB 1047 falls short in Senate
item.description: Oklahoma tribal sports betting stalls again as HB 1047 dies in the Senate amid Gov. Stitt's push for a multi-operator market over tribal exclusivity.

item.title: Scugog Island First Nation enters mediation with Ontario over iGaming
item.description: The Mississaugas of Scugog Island First Nation are heading to mediation with Ontario, arguing the province's iGaming launch breached a 2016 deal and the duty to consult.

item.title: How institutional capital is reshaping tribal casino financing
item.description: Tribal casino financing is drawing REITs and large credit syndicates in 2026, even as sovereignty and trust-land rules keep the deals structurally distinct.

item.title: Inside California's tribal gaming economy, the nation's largest market
item.description: California tribal gaming adds roughly $20 billion to the state economy and supports about 125,000 jobs, anchoring the country's largest Indian gaming market in 2026.

item.title: What 'hub-and-spoke' means for tribal sports betting, explained
item.description: The hub-and-spoke model lets tribes offer statewide mobile sports betting by routing every wager through servers on tribal land. Here's how it works and why it spread.

item.title: North Fork Mono Casino nears fall 2026 opening near Madera
item.description: The North Fork Rancheria's $725 million Madera resort is on track for a fall 2026 opening after two decades of legal and political delays.

item.title: Ho-Chunk Nation's $705M Beloit casino targets September opening
item.description: Ho-Chunk Gaming Beloit is on track for a September 2026 opening, intensifying cross-border competition with Hard Rock Casino Rockford.

item.title: How sweepstakes casino bans reinforce tribal gaming exclusivity
item.description: A wave of state sweepstakes casino bans in 2026 has handed tribes a win on exclusivity—and a new question about recouping past profits.

item.title: The off-reservation gaming wave reshaping where casinos rise
item.description: From Madera to Kings Mountain, tribes are increasingly building casinos far from ancestral lands—reviving old legal fights over IGRA.

item.title: Pechanga Resort Casino: profile of the West Coast's largest
item.description: A profile of Pechanga Resort Casino and the Pechanga Band of Luiseno Indians—the largest casino resort on the U.S. West Coast.

item.title: Newsom signs AB 1389, extending Yurok Tribe gaming compact through 2026
item.description: California ratified a one-year extension of the Yurok Tribe gaming compact, keeping the Redwood Hotel & Casino operating while longer-term talks continue.

item.title: Federal judge lets Ho-Chunk Nation's IGRA claims against Kalshi proceed
item.description: A Wisconsin federal judge ruled the Ho-Chunk Nation can pursue IGRA claims against Kalshi, the first such ruling against a prediction-market operator.

item.title: From revenue share to ownership: Indigenous operators reshape Canadian gaming
item.description: Pure Casino Entertainment's bid for Gamehost marks a shift as Indigenous-owned operators move from revenue-sharing recipients to outright owners of commercial casinos.

item.title: Tribal gaming's 2026 challenge: flat revenue, rising costs, tighter margins
item.description: Analysts expect a sideways economy in 2026, pressuring tribal casino margins as costs rise and aging facilities compete for limited capital.

item.title: Secretarial Procedures: what happens when compact talks break down
item.description: When a tribe and state can't reach a Class III gaming compact, federal law provides a fallback. Here's how Secretarial Procedures work under IGRA.

item.title: Maine's Wabanaki Nations Defend Exclusive Online Gaming Law
item.description: Maine's four Wabanaki Nations hold exclusive online gaming rights under LD 1164, but a Churchill Downs lawsuit now tests tribal economic sovereignty in court.

item.title: Choctaw Durant Unveils the Largest Non-Smoking Casino Floor
item.description: Choctaw Casino & Resort in Durant has completed a phased Grand Casino refresh, unveiling what the operator calls the largest non-smoking gaming floor in the U.S.

item.title: Kahnawake's Gaming Model Tested by Canada's Regulated Markets
item.description: The Kahnawake Gaming Commission built a sovereignty-based online gaming regime in the 1990s. Provincial regulated markets are now reshaping its place in Canada.

item.title: Why Tribal Casinos Are Building All at Once in 2026
item.description: From Coushatta's Legacy Tower to Graton's expansion, 2026 has become a banner year for tribal casino construction. A look at the capital cycle driving the boom.

item.title: Land Into Trust and Section 20: When Tribes Can Game on New Land
item.description: A plain-English explainer on the fee-to-trust process and IGRA Section 20 — the rules that decide whether a tribe can offer gaming on newly acquired land.

item.title: Graton Rancheria opens phase one of $1B Sonoma County expansion
item.description: Federated Indians of Graton Rancheria opened 144,000 sq ft of new gaming space, 2,000 slots and four dining venues on May 4 — phase one of a $1B build-out.

item.title: Mohegan Tribe closes acquisition of WNBA's Connecticut Sun
item.description: Mohegan Tribal Gaming Authority has closed its purchase of the Connecticut Sun, giving the tribe a marquee WNBA franchise as it diversifies beyond gaming.

item.title: NIGC's $43.9B record, one year on: what FY 2024 really showed
item.description: A year after the NIGC's record FY 2024 GGR report, the structural story is market concentration: 9% of operations are generating 55% of tribal gaming revenue.

item.title: Tribal Labor Sovereignty Act 2025: the NLRB jurisdiction question, explained
item.description: H.R. 1723 and S. 1301 would exclude tribal enterprises from NLRA coverage. Here's how the bills sit against 20+ years of NLRB jurisdiction over tribal gaming.

item.title: Manitoba's First Nations casino network: a regional overview
item.description: An orientation to Manitoba's six First Nations casinos — South Beach, Aseneskak, Sand Hills, Niichi and the Swan Lake centres — and how the province's model compares.

item.title: Mashpee Wampanoag chart financing path for permanent First Light resort
item.description: After a year of temporary operations, the Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe is recalibrating financing for a scaled-down permanent First Light Resort & Casino in Massachusetts.

item.title: Pokagon Band launches Four Winds Ventures to chase commercial gaming growth
item.description: The Pokagon Band's new Four Winds Ventures arm signals a deliberate tribal pivot toward commercial gaming investment, both domestically and abroad.

item.title: Ontario's OFNLP keeps quietly redirecting gaming revenue to 132 First Nations
item.description: The Ontario First Nations Limited Partnership channels roughly $170 million a year to 132 First Nations — a model that contrasts sharply with Alberta and B.C.

item.title: North Carolina sports betting at two years: the Eastern Band Cherokee model in focus
item.description: Two years into legalization, North Carolina's $8 billion mobile handle highlights the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians' commercial partnership model with Caesars.

item.title: Yaamava' and the San Manuel enterprise: a benchmark for tribal gaming at scale
item.description: The Yuhaaviatam of San Manuel Nation's Yaamava' Resort and Palms acquisition position the tribe as one of the most strategically deliberate tribal operators in North America.

item.title: Minnesota's tribal-led mobile sports betting bill enters final weeks
item.description: SF 4139 would route Minnesota online sports betting through eleven tribes at a 22% tax rate — with the May 18 legislative adjournment looming.

item.title: Washington weighs multi-operator tribal sportsbooks under HB 2526
item.description: HB 2526 would let each Washington tribal casino partner with multiple sportsbook brands and extend on-site wagering to in-state college games.

item.title: Tribal casinos confront a ransomware epidemic — and rewrite playbooks
item.description: Back-to-back RansomHub attacks on Lower Sioux and Sault Tribe operations have pushed tribal gaming cybersecurity from IT concern to council-level governance.

item.title: Comparing First Nations gaming revenue frameworks across Canada
item.description: Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Ontario, Alberta, and BC each share gaming revenue with First Nations differently — and the iGaming era is widening the gaps.

item.title: Inside the Pacific Northwest tribal gaming market — Washington and Oregon
item.description: Twenty-nine Washington casinos and nine Oregon casinos run a retail-only, compact-disciplined model that has quietly defined the Pacific Northwest.

item.title: NIGC Halts Grand Traverse Band's Benzie Parcel Gaming Over Indian Lands Status
item.description: The NIGC's first 2026 enforcement action, NOV-26-01, halts Grand Traverse Band gaming on a Michigan parcel found ineligible under IGRA's Indian lands test.

item.title: Alabama-Coushatta to Open Temporary Casino as Permanent Texas Resort Breaks Ground
item.description: The Alabama-Coushatta Tribe will open a 300-machine temporary casino in Leggett, Texas this summer with permanent resort construction starting June 18, 2026.

item.title: Tribal Cashless Gaming Adoption Trails Forecasts as Operators Stay Cautious in 2026
item.description: Tribal operators discussed cashless gaming progress at IGA 2026, but adoption remains well below vendor forecasts as Resorts World's pullback raises questions.

item.title: California HHR Standoff: Santa Anita Terminals Test Tribal Slot Exclusivity
item.description: Santa Anita's January 2026 HHR rollout has revived a California tribal gaming dispute over whether historical horse racing machines infringe slot exclusivity.

item.title: Inside the Choctaw Nation: Profile of a Top US Tribal Gaming Enterprise
item.description: A profile of the Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma's gaming enterprise, including the 2026 Wyndham hotel partnership and Durant's smoke-free conversion.

item.title: Oneida Nation accelerates Turning Stone Crescent Hotel debut
item.description: The Oneida Indian Nation will open Turning Stone's $370 million Crescent Hotel and Grand Expo ahead of schedule in 2026, deepening New York tribal gaming.

item.title: Wisconsin signs tribal-led mobile sports betting bill into law
item.description: Governor Tony Evers signed Wisconsin's tribal hub-and-spoke mobile sports betting law, making the state the 33rd to legalize online wagering under IGRA.

item.title: Bill S-241 puts First Nations gaming jurisdiction back before the Senate
item.description: Bill S-241 would amend Canada's Criminal Code to recognize First Nations' exclusive authority to license and regulate gaming on reserve lands.

item.title: Shakopee Mdewakanton broaden gaming empire with Mystic Lake Amphitheater
item.description: The Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community's 19,000-seat Mystic Lake Amphitheater opens in summer 2026, anchoring a wave of tribal entertainment diversification.

item.title: What revenue sharing really means in a tribal-state gaming compact
item.description: Tribal-state compact revenue sharing is exchanged for gaming exclusivity. Here's how the rates, triggers, and trust-fund flows actually work under IGRA.

item.title: Coushatta Casino Resort opens Legacy Tower in Louisiana expansion
item.description: The Coushatta Tribe of Louisiana opened its 204-room Legacy Tower this month, capping the most significant capital project in the resort's 30-year history.

item.title: California tribes formally defer sports betting ballot to 2028
item.description: California's gaming tribes have ruled out a 2026 sports-betting ballot, citing intra-tribal coalition work and a need to settle revenue-sharing with non-gaming tribes first.

item.title: DOI Part 293, two years in: how the new compact rules reshaped tribal-state talks
item.description: The Department of the Interior's 2024 update to 25 C.F.R. Part 293 has quietly become one of the most consequential federal actions on tribal gaming in a decade.

item.title: British Columbia's First Nations casino buyouts: a quiet ownership shift
item.description: Eight commercial casinos in southwest British Columbia have transferred to First Nations ownership in two years, reshaping Canadian gaming structure.

item.title: Beyond the casinos: how the Chickasaw Nation built a diversified enterprise
item.description: The Chickasaw Nation operates 18 Oklahoma casinos and more than 100 other businesses. The non-gaming portfolio is where the tribe's long game shows up.

item.title: Catawba Two Kings Casino opens first phase of $1B North Carolina resort
item.description: The Catawba Nation opened phase one of its $1 billion Two Kings Casino Resort in Kings Mountain, North Carolina — 1,350 slots, 22 tables, sports betting kiosks.

item.title: New Mexico tribes sue Kalshi, alleging IGRA violations on tribal lands
item.description: Four New Mexico tribes filed federal suit against Kalshi, arguing the platform's sports event contracts are unauthorized Class III gaming under IGRA.

item.title: Alberta iGaming launches July 13 — what 2% revenue sharing means for First Nations
item.description: Alberta's regulated iGaming market opens July 13, 2026, with 28 operators and a 2% gross revenue allocation to First Nations. A closer look at the framework.

item.title: Prediction markets and tribal exclusivity — IGRA's biggest 2026 stress test
item.description: Tribal lawsuits against Kalshi and Polymarket have made prediction markets the most consequential challenge to IGRA exclusivity in 2026. An analysis.

item.title: Class II vs Class III tribal gaming — what the IGRA distinction actually means
item.description: Class II vs Class III gaming under IGRA is one of the most consequential distinctions in tribal gaming law. A clear, operator-focused explainer.

item.title: Inside the Seminole Compact: How one 30-year deal reshaped American sports betting
item.description: An exclusive analysis of the hub-and-spoke framework now drawing legal challenges in four other states — and why tribal attorneys say IGRA has always anticipated this moment.

item.title: Tribal gaming generated $138B in total economic output in 2025, new report finds
item.description: The most comprehensive joint AGA–NIGA assessment to date.

item.title: SIGA announces seventh property as Saskatchewan First Nations drive provincial gaming
item.description: The Saskatchewan Indian Gaming Authority remains the dominant model for First Nations gaming in Canada.
